description: Under the manuscript's structural inputs, the regular, genuinely nonbinary quadratic-source, simple-, double-, fourth-, and fifth-ramification strata are closed; the only primitive binary calculation still open is the exceptional triple-ramification F4 family.

independent_review.scope: No independent review is represented in this public record.

manuscript_coverage.coverage_rule: Complete coverage requires an exact LaTeX location for every program-relevant defining claim. A locator records where the current statement and evidence boundary appear; it is not a proof-review status.

members.statement: Subject to the leading-curve reductions in the Program 2 manuscript, any nonautomorphic quartic Keller map in three variables has leading target span exactly two.
members.title: Every Quartic Counterexample Has Leading Target Span Two

members.statement: In the binary target-span-two locus, if U=J(Q,R), V=J(P,R), and W=J(P,Q) are all nonzero and gcd(U,V,W)=1, then the quartic Keller map is a polynomial automorphism.
members.title: Regular Binary Quartic Pencils Are Automorphic

members.statement: No quartic Keller map belongs to the genuinely nonbinary, no-fixed-component quadratic-source locus of the target-span-two reduction.
members.title: The Nonbinary Quadratic-Source Locus Is Empty

members.statement: Assuming the Program 2 structural inputs, a quartic Keller map in the coprime binary-pencil locus is a polynomial automorphism whenever deg gcd(J(Q,R),J(P,R),J(P,Q)) is at most one.
members.title: Simple Binary Ramification Is Automorphic

members.statement: Assuming the Program 2 structural inputs, a quartic Keller map in the coprime binary-pencil locus is a polynomial automorphism whenever deg gcd(J(Q,R),J(P,R),J(P,Q)) is at most two.
members.title: Double Binary Ramification Is Automorphic

members.statement: Assuming the Program 2 structural inputs, in the coprime binary-pencil locus with ramification divisor of degree three, the type-(2,5) and generic type-(3,4) Hilbert--Burch branches are automorphic or enter previously excluded cube, fourth-power, fixed-component, or source-shear boundaries; any remaining generic normal deformation lies on the explicit F4 weighted-inflection family.
members.title: Triple Binary Ramification Reduces to an Explicit Weighted-Inflection Family

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 structural reductions place a quartic Keller map in the primitive coprime binary-pencil locus, with H4=(P,Q,0), P,Q in k[x,y]_4 coprime, R=(H3)_3 in k[x,y]_3, U=J(Q,R), V=J(P,R), W=J(P,Q), and r=deg gcd(U,V,W). If r is four or five, then the full Keller map is a polynomial automorphism.
members.title: Primitive Binary Ramification Four and Five Is Automorphic

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 target-span-two reductions and suppose a primitive coprime leading pencil contains a fourth power, normalized as H4=(x^4,Q,0) with x not dividing Q. The highest Keller equation routes the cubic and, when necessary, quadratic normal layers to an aligned pure-power, binary, or quadratic-source branch; under the recorded Program 2 inputs every resulting branch is automorphic or already excluded.
members.title: The Primitive Fourth-Power Locus Adds No Quartic Counterexample Leaf

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 binary target-span-two reduction. If one of U=J(Q,R), V=J(P,R), or W=J(P,Q) vanishes, including the separate case R=0, then the quartic Keller map is a polynomial automorphism. Consequently the ordinary common-ramification filtration may be applied only after these zero-minor boundaries are removed.
members.title: Zero-Minor Binary Quartic Boundaries Are Automorphic

members.statement: In the primitive fixed-component branch P=GA, Q=GB with gcd(A,B)=1 and R=(H3)_3, write t=A/B and R^4/Q^3=rho(t). If an irreducible component Gamma occurs in G with multiplicity s and in the reduced special fiber A-xi B with multiplicity m, define c_xi=ord_xi(rho) for finite xi and c_infinity=ord_infinity(rho)+3. Then 4 nu_Gamma(R)=3s+c_xi m and the coefficients satisfy sum c_xi=3.
members.title: Corrected Valuation Identity for Primitive Quartic Fixed Components

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 four-loci reduction and the standard polynomial-centralizer theorem used in the proof note. Every genuinely nonbinary primitive fixed-component branch is closed: a fixed factor of degree two is eliminated by the corrected valuation identity or enters the existing same-fiber rank-one chart, while a fixed factor of degree one is aligned-automorphic, binary, or incompatible with the Keller condition.
members.title: Genuinely Nonbinary Primitive Fixed Components Are Closed

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 reductions reach a binary leading pencil whose greatest common divisor has degree three. After normalization H4=(xG,yG,0) with G in k[x,y]_3, every multiplicity type of G and every cubic R=(H3)_3 yields a polynomial automorphism or a triangular degree drop; hence this stratum contains no counterexample.
members.title: Binary Cubic Fixed Factors Are Automorphic

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 reductions reach a binary leading pencil whose greatest common divisor is a line. After normalization H4=(x^4,xB,0), with B a binary cubic not divisible by x, every quartic Keller map in the stratum is a polynomial automorphism.
members.title: Binary Linear Fixed Factors Are Automorphic

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 reductions reach a binary leading pencil H4=(P,Q,0) whose greatest common divisor G has degree two and whose residual binary quadrics are coprime. Then the residual pencil is a secant of the Veronese conic and may be normalized to P=x^2G, Q=y^2G; the generic first-normal complement and all four exceptional divisors QF1 through QF4 contain no counterexample, so the full Keller map is a polynomial automorphism.
members.title: Binary Quadratic Fixed Factors Are Automorphic

title: The Quartic Target-Span-Two Ramification Filtration
